case_number: Civil Appeal No. 5822 of 2022 (arising out of SLP (C) No. 13565 of 2021)

parties.respondent: Siddamsetty Infra Projects Pvt. Ltd. & Ors.

summary: The case involved a dispute over specific performance of two agreements dated 26.03.1997 and 27.03.1997 for the sale of 40.08 gts. of land. The purchaser paid 90% of the consideration but failed to pay the balance within the stipulated 3 months. The trial court dismissed the suit, citing lack of readiness, unclean hands, and limitation. The High Court reversed, holding that time was not the essence of the contract, the purchaser was ready and willing, had deposited the balance amount in court, and was in possession. The Supreme Court upheld the High Court's judgment, emphasizing the purchaser's bonafides and the discretionary relief of specific performance.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 10 of the Specific Relief Act (as substituted by Act 18 of 2018)
final_judgment: The appeal was allowed, and the High Court's judgment directing specific performance of the agreements was upheld. The vendors were directed to execute a registered sale deed upon receipt of the balance consideration deposited in court.
